recentItems.title: Israel's New Apache Attack Helicopters: Big Hamas Meltdown, Hezbollah's End Confirmed| IDF Firepower
recentItems.description:
Iran and its proxies, like Hamas in Gaza and Hezbollah in Lebanon...The Israeli Military is tackling threats at multiple fronts and dominating each battle arena.

The Israeli Ministry of Defense announced that it is moving forward with an agreement to purchase 12 advanced Apache attack helicopters from American aerospace manufacturer Boeing, following approval by the Israeli government.

Israeli Ministry of Defense Director General Amir Baram instructed the ministry's mission to the United States to sign the agreement with the Pentagon.

The helicopters will be the AH64-E Apache, also known as the 'Echo' variant, the newest and most advanced version of the attack helicopter.

According to the Defense Ministry, the agreement was developed through a joint Israeli-American effort to meet Israel's specific defense requirements.

Defense Minister Israel Katz welcomed the agreement, describing it as a significant investment in the IDF's future operational capabilities.

recentItems.description:

recentItems.description:

Even the farmers’ unions have come forward in support of Parvinder’s family.

recentItems.title: Iran Blows Up A Crushing X Move With Vow To Cut Off Smuggled Starlink Ahead of Key US Midterms
recentItems.description:
Iran’s state-imposed internet shutdowns have created a compounding crisis in the information environment. 

The shutdowns are used as both a censorship tool and a content strategy designed to silence authentic Iranian voices and project a single state-sanctioned narrative to the outside world. 

This strategy was made explicit when Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared live on American television that he is the voice of Iranians, with internet access granted to him exclusively as the Islamic Republic’s designated spokesperson while millions of others remain cut off.

The influx of 50000-100000 Starlink terminals offered a narrow window into the January uprising and the current war, but smuggling hardware into a country of over 90 million people is not a solution.
